newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods slip with NYMEX, but Gulf heat firms.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods slip with NYMEX, but Gulf heat firms.

text.p: U.S. spot refinery product prices slipped Monday morning on NYMEX futures, although Gulf Coast distillate differentials continued to firm on keen refiner buying, traders said.
USG heating oil was sold for 1.0 cent below March futures, about 0.30 cent firmer than late Friday values, with front fourth-cycle low sulfur diesel selling for 1.25 cents over -- a half cent firmer.
"Refiners are in buying again, particularly on jet fuel," one Gulf player said, adding distillate supplies have tightened in recent weeks as refiners have opted toward stronger gasoline production.
Gulf 54-grade jet fuel was offered at about 2.0 cents over the print, 0.40 cent firmer than Friday diffs, players said, with low-sulfur 55 grade offered at 3.0 cents over.
In New York Harbor, distillate diffs eased slightly, with heating oil heard sold for 1.60 cents over the screen, with jet fuel diffs holding stable at Friday levels, players said.
NYH conventional unleaded gasoline, meanwhile, was talked slightly lower at about 2.0 cents under the March print, players said, amid expected higher-than-normal import volumes.
